Dan Gilbert was born on January 17, 1962.
Dan Gilbert is from Detroit, Michigan.
Dan Gilbert grew up in Southfield, Michigan.
Dan Gilbert attended Southfield-Lathrup High School.
Dan Gilbert earned his bachelor's degree from Michigan State University.
Dan Gilbert earned a Juris Doctor from Wayne State University Law School.
Dan Gilbert is a member of the State Bar of Michigan.
Dan Gilbert earned a real estate agent's license while in college.
Dan Gilbert worked part-time at his parents' Century 21 Real Estate agency during law school.
Dan Gilbert co-founded Rock Financial with Ron Berman, Lindsay Gross and Gary Gilbert in 1985.
Rock Financial launched its internet strategy in the late 1990s.
Rock Financial became an early online direct mortgage lender in the late 1990s.
In the fourth quarter of 2017, Rock Financial became the largest retail mortgage lender by volume in the United States.
In 2000, Intuit Inc. purchased Rock Financial and renamed it Quicken Loans.
In 2002, Dan Gilbert and a group of private investors purchased Quicken Loans from Intuit Inc.
As of 2021, Dan Gilbert was the chairman of Quicken Loans, Inc.
In 2007, Dan Gilbert and the city of Detroit announced an agreement to move Rock Financial's headquarters to downtown Detroit.
All 3,600 Michigan-based employees moved into Detroit's urban core by the end of 2010.
In August 2020, Quicken Loans went public under the name Rocket Companies.
In 2020, Dan Gilbert remained the majority owner of Rocket Companies with control over 79% of the company's shares.
Dan Gilbert bought the Cleveland Cavaliers for $375 million in 2005.
Since buying the Cleveland Cavaliers, Dan Gilbert has overseen significant improvements to the team's facilities.
Dan Gilbert helped bring top players like LeBron James to the Cleveland Cavaliers.
In 2006, Dan Gilbert purchased the Cleveland Monsters, a professional ice hockey team in the American Hockey League.
The Cleveland Monsters are affiliated with the NHL's Columbus Blue Jackets.
Dan Gilbert has been an active and vocal owner of his teams.
Dan Gilbert has spoken out on social media and in public about his teams and the NBA.
Dan Gilbert has been involved in efforts to bring major sporting events to Cleveland, including the NBA All-Star Game and the NFL Draft.
The Cleveland Cavaliers won their first NBA championship in 2016 under Dan Gilbert's ownership.
After LeBron James left in 2018, the Cleveland Cavaliers went through a tumultuous period.
Dan Gilbert has faced criticism for his treatment of former head coach David Blatt.
Dan Gilbert has been aggressive in pursuing tax incentives and public funding for his various business ventures in Cleveland.
Dan Gilbert is a founding partner in Rockbridge Growth Equity LLC (RBE).
Rockbridge Growth Equity LLC invests in growing businesses in the financial services, Internet technology, consumer-direct marketing, and sports and entertainment industries.
Rockbridge Growth Equity LLC has significant investments in Gas Station TV, Robb Report, and RapidAdvance.
Dan Gilbert is an investor in Courtside Ventures, a venture capital fund investing across early-stage technology and media companies with a focus on sports.
Dan Gilbert is a founding partner of Detroit Venture Partners (DVP), a venture capital firm that funds start-up and early-stage technology companies based primarily in Detroit.
Some of the companies DVP has invested in include LevelEleven, iRule, and Marxent Labs.
Dan Gilbert cofounded StockX, a stock market of things for high-demand, limited edition products such as sneakers.
Dan Gilbert is involved in several consumer-based technology-centered businesses including Fathead, Veritix, Xenith, StyleCaster, and Quizzle.
Dan Gilbert launched nonprofit Bizdom in 2007 to promote tech and brick-and-mortar entrepreneurship in Detroit and Cleveland by supporting on-the-ground service providers.
In November 2009, Dan Gilbert successfully backed a statewide referendum to bring casino gaming to Ohio's four largest cities.
Through a joint venture with Caesars Entertainment Corporation, the groups operate urban-based casinos in both Cleveland and Cincinnati.
The first of the casinos, Jack Cleveland Casino, opened in May 2012.

In 2013, Rock Ventures, Gilbert's umbrella entity for investments and real estate holdings, announced it had formed Athens Acquisition LLC, an affiliate of Rock Gaming, and acquired the majority interest in Greektown Superholdings Inc., owner of the Greektown Casino-Hotel located in downtown Detroit.
In late 2018, Dan Gilbert bought the online dictionaries, Dictionary.com and Thesaurus.com.
In November 2017, Matthew "Nadeshot" Haag announced that Dan Gilbert had made a multimillion-dollar investment into the esports organization 100 Thieves.
Quicken Loans moved its headquarters to downtown Detroit in August 2010.
Gilbert and Quicken Loans are helping lead a revitalization of Detroit's urban core.

Bedrock Detroit, an entity owned by Dan Gilbert, has purchased several buildings in downtown Detroit including the historic Madison Theatre Building, Chase Tower, Two Detroit Center, Dime Building, the First National Building, the David Stott Building, and the former Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Detroit Branch Building.
Bedrock Detroit has also purchased several buildings on Woodward Avenue including One Woodward Avenue and the 1001 Woodward office tower.
In September 2013, Dan Gilbert was named co-chair of the Blight Removal Task Force.
The group published a detailed plan in May 2014 to remove all blighted structures and lots in the City of Detroit.
In 2015, Dan Gilbert purchased Book Tower in Detroit for $30 million.
A 2017 Politico Magazine article named Dan Gilbert one of "America's 11 Most Interesting Mayors" due to his role in the city's development.
In September 2017, Detroit Mayor Mike Duggan appointed Dan Gilbert to lead a committee to make a bid for Amazon to bring its second North American headquarters to Detroit.
Amazon narrowed its list of potential headquarters locations and removed Detroit from its list of contenders.
Dan Gilbert and his wife Jennifer joined The Giving Pledge in September 2012, committing to give half of their wealth to philanthropy throughout their lifetimes.

Jennifer Gilbert is on the Gilbert Family Neurofibromatosis Institute at Children's National Medical Center in Washington, D.C., and on the boards of ORT America and the Israeli and Overseas Committee of the Jewish Federation of Metropolitan Detroit.

Dan Gilbert established two neurofibromatosis research clinics at the Children's National Medical Center (CNMC) in Washington, D.C., and at the Dana Children's Hospital at the Sourasky Medical Center in Tel Aviv, Israel.
Dan Gilbert is on the boards of the Children's Tumor Foundation, the Cleveland Clinic, and the Children's Hospital Foundation (an affiliate of CNMC).
Dan Gilbert is the vice-chairman of the not-for-profit M-1 RAIL initiative which promotes light-rail transportation in downtown Detroit.
In 2015, Dan Gilbert donated $750,000 to Chris Christie's presidential candidacy.
In September 2016, Dan Gilbert donated $5 million to Wayne State University Law School.
In October 2016, Dan Gilbert also donated $15 million toward the planned $50-million Breslin Center renovation project at Michigan State University.
In 2020, Dan Gilbert made a $1.2 million donation to help COVID-19 relief efforts in Detroit.
Dan Gilbert resides in Michigan with his wife Jennifer Gilbert.

Jennifer Gilbert is on the Gilbert Family Neurofibromatosis Institute at Children's National Medical Center in Washington, D.C., and on the boards of ORT America and the Israeli and Overseas Committee of the Jewish Federation of Metropolitan Detroit.
On May 26, 2019, Dan Gilbert was taken to the hospital and treated for a stroke at the age of 57.
Dan Gilbert's eldest son Nick died on May 6, 2023, after a long battle with neurofibromatosis.
